transcript:
[doctor] Hi, how are you doing today? What brings you in?

[patient] Hi, I'm alright, but I've been having some trouble with constipation for the past 3 weeks.

[doctor] Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. How severe has it been?

[patient] It's been moderate, but it's happening every day. It's really starting to bother me.

[doctor] I see. Are you experiencing any other symptoms along with the constipation?

[patient] Yes, I feel bloated and have some abdominal discomfort.

[doctor] Hmm, okay. Anything else you've noticed?

[patient] No, just the bloating and discomfort. It's also making it hard for me to concentrate at work.

[doctor] Alright, let's go over a few more details. Have you had any fever, chills, or weight loss recently?

[patient] No, none of those.

[doctor] Any blood in your stool or black, tarry stools?

[patient] No, nothing like that.

[doctor] How about any urinary symptoms?

[patient] No, everything's normal there.

[doctor] Any chest pain or palpitations?

[patient] No, my heart feels fine.

[doctor] Any shortness of breath or cough?

[patient] No, my breathing is normal.

[doctor] Have you had any headaches or dizziness?

[patient] No, none.

[doctor] How's your sleep been?

[patient] It's been interrupted, but I'm not feeling depressed or anxious.

[doctor] Okay, thank you for sharing all that. Let's check your vitals. Your blood pressure is 128/76 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, temperature is 98.6°F, oxygen saturation is 99%, and your respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute. All of these look good.

[patient] That's good to hear.

[doctor] Now, let's do a physical exam. I see you’re well-nourished and in no acute distress. Your abdomen shows mild tenderness in the lower area, but there are no palpable masses, and your bowel sounds are normal. No hepatosplenomegaly.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] Your cardiovascular exam shows a regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Respiratory exam is clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. Neurologically, you are alert and oriented, and your cranial nerves II-XII are grossly intact. Your skin shows no rashes or lesions.

[patient] Alright, what does all this mean?

[doctor] Based on your symptoms and physical exam, it looks like you have constipation. To help with this, I recommend increasing your dietary fiber intake through fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. 

[patient] Okay, I can try that.

[doctor] I also want to start you on polyethylene glycol 3350, which is commonly known as Miralax. You’ll take 17 grams of the powder mixed in 4-8 ounces of beverage, once daily for 14 days.

[patient] Got it. Anything else I should do?

[doctor] Yes, make sure to increase your physical activity and stay well-hydrated. These lifestyle changes can really help with constipation.

[patient] I'll do my best.

[doctor] I've ordered a complete blood count (CBC) and basic metabolic panel (BMP) to rule out any underlying issues like electrolyte imbalances or anemia. We’ll wait for those results.

[patient] Alright, when will I know the results?

[doctor] The results should be available within a few days. We’ll discuss them during your follow-up visit.

[patient] Okay, when should I schedule the follow-up?

[doctor] Let's schedule a follow-up visit in 2 weeks to assess your response to the treatment.

[patient] Sounds good.

[doctor] If you have any concerns or if your symptoms worsen, please contact me immediately.

[patient] I will. Thank you.

[doctor] Before you go, I want to stress the importance of adhering to the dietary changes and medication regimen. Fiber supplements can be very effective, but they need to be taken consistently.

[patient] Understood. I'll make sure to follow everything you’ve suggested.

[doctor] Great. Do you have any other questions or concerns?

[patient] No, that covers it. Thank you for your help.

[doctor] You're welcome. Take care, and I'll see you in 2 weeks.

[patient] Thank you, bye.

[doctor] Bye.
